Two weeks after engineering shipped a change, read the results. Be careful: small numbers, short window.

Engineering change ENG-4471: When a charger reconnects while the backend holds an open transaction on it, the backend asks the charger (GetTransactionStatus) and keeps the transaction open while messages are queued. Events are keyed on the station, transactionId and seqNo, and applied once, in seqNo order, whatever the EVSE status. The backend closes a transaction provisionally, at its own last recorded meter value, only when the charger reports it is not ongoing with nothing queued, the event sequence has no gaps, and recorded energy is flat; the invoice is then marked provisional for billing review. Anything else (energy still rising, no ongoing report, a sequence gap, or a newer transaction on the same EVSE) goes to a person. A late Ended after a provisional close replaces the provisional values once and does not create a second charge.
Rollout: Behind a per-station flag on 5 canary sites running FW-B 4.2.x; 6 control sites (4 FW-B, 2 FW-A) stay on the old behaviour, so the control is not perfectly matched. Firmware vendor ticket opened for FW-B behaviour after reconnect; still open.

Results over 14 days before and 14 days after:
- Canary (5 FW-B sites, change on): before 6 drops near unplug, 5 stuck sessions. After 6 drops near unplug, 0 stuck, 5 closed by reconciliation.
- Control (6 FW-B sites, change off): before 5 drops, 4 stuck. After 6 drops, 4 stuck.
- Support detector: 4 hits on control sites, all 4 ticketed before any complaint, median 31 min to flag. Before the detector, median time to first complaint was 6.2 hours.
- Correctness on canary sites (2140 sessions): 5 reconciled; 0 closed a transaction still delivering energy; 1 skipped because a newer transaction had started; 3 late Ended events arrived and 3 were applied once; 0 duplicate charges; 5 provisional invoices reviewed, 1 adjusted.

Hypotheses under test: the backend ignores an Ended event that arrives after the EVSE reports Available (seen in a log); FW-B does not send its queued Ended event after reconnect (inferred from its absence). They may coexist.

- reading: 2 sentences, under 50 words in total.
- what_it_does_not_prove: 3 bullets, each under 20 words.
- keep_watching: 2 bullets, each under 15 words.
- next_decision: one or two sentences, under 50 words in all. With samples this small, weigh continuing observation against widening the rollout. State the bar for widening as a minimum observation period and a minimum number of drops near unplug on the canary, and say what would reverse the decision.

data.reading: Canary stuck sessions fell from 5 to 0 while drops stayed at 6; control stayed at 4 stuck. Five were closed by reconciliation, none while energy was still flowing. Direction fits the backend-ignores-late-Ended hypothesis, but counts are tiny.
what_it_does_not_prove: That FW-B fails to send queued Ended; 3 late Ended events arrived, so absence is only partial.
That the fix generalises beyond 5 canary sites on FW-B 4.2.x.

keep_watching: Any closure while energy still rising; late Ended applied twice.

data.next_decision: Keep the canary running; do not widen yet. Bar: at least 28 more days and at least 10 further drops near unplug on canary with 0 early closures or duplicate charges. Any such event, or stuck sessions returning, reverses it.

impact: 14 tickets across 9 sites and two firmware lines in 21 days
Idle fees kept running on open sessions; drivers and a fleet manager dispute them
A driver was blocked from starting a new session at another site

evidence.point: On CP-014-02 the connector reconnected and reported Available, but the backend still held the session as Charging with no Ended.
evidence.quote: state=Charging  last_meter=18.42 kWh  (no TransactionEvent Ended received)

evidence.point: On CP-031-01 the same sequence appeared after an EVCommunicationLost update and a websocket drop, and the map then showed the charger in use.
evidence.quote: CP-031-01 shown 'In use' (derived from open session)

evidence.point: On CP-022-04 an Ended did arrive after reconnect, but the backend ignored it because the connector was already Available.
evidence.quote: ignored: connector already Available (out of order)

evidence.point: On FW-B 4.2.x, 12 of 19 drops within 90 s of unplug got stuck; 41 drops at other times got none stuck.

hypotheses.statement: The backend ignores a late Ended that arrives after the connector is already Available, leaving the session open. This mechanism is seen directly in one log.
supports: CP-022-04 log shows the backend ignoring a late Ended as out of order.
Stuck cases cluster on drops within 90 s of unplug, around the reconnect.
against_or_gaps: Only one of three logs shows an Ended arriving and being ignored.
Not known whether the ignore rule is applied the same way for other firmware.

hypotheses.statement: The charger never sends or never queues the Ended after an unplug-time drop, so the backend has nothing to close the session with.
supports: CP-014-02 and CP-031-01 logs show no Ended after reconnect.
FW-B 4.2.x has the highest stuck rate: 12 of 19 drops.
against_or_gaps: A missing line at the gateway could be a capture or logging gap.
CP-022-04 (FW-A) did send an Ended, so both mechanisms may coexist.

ruled_out: Payment provider fault is unlikely: no incidents logged and normal captures on unaffected sessions.
App display bug is unlikely: the session API itself returns state=Charging.
A single bad site or charger is unlikely: 14 tickets across 9 sites.
Driver behaviour is unlikely: every affected connector reported Available within 2 minutes of unplug.
open_questions: Does the charger store and resend Ended after an unplug-time drop on FW-B 4.2.x?

Could the gateway have missed Ended messages in the CP-014-02 and CP-031-01 logs?

- title: a ticket title, at most 10 words.
- scope: one sentence with counts of tickets, sites, firmware lines and days.
- rules_triggered: which escalation rules apply.
- reproduction: 4 steps, each under 24 words. Start with running the lab's reproduction test with the fix flag off (see "Lab" below), then what its result shows: it passes by asserting the bug (the transaction stays open). Keep exactly one manual step for the open firmware question: on a FW-B 4.2.x test charger, drop the connection after EVCommunicationLost but before the Ended event is sent, with capture at both the charger and the gateway.
- evidence_attached: 5 items, each under 12 words, the first being "Lab tests: bug reproduced; regression fails without the fix". No long lists of ids.
- ruled_out: 4 causes judged unlikely, each with its reason, each under 14 words. Do not call any cause impossible.
- workaround_in_place: one sentence under 30 words.
- the_ask: the single specific decision engineering is asked to make, under 40 words.
- hypothesis_note: use exactly: "The backend ignoring a late Ended is reproduced in a lab with a simulated charger. Whether FW-B drops its queued Ended is not confirmed."

Escalation rules:
code: Needs a code, firmware or production config change
spread: Same pattern at 3+ sites, or recurring for 2+ weeks
billing: Billing or session data correctness at risk
safety: Any safety concern

Engineering change: When a charger reconnects while the backend holds an open transaction on it, the backend asks the charger (GetTransactionStatus) and keeps the transaction open while messages are queued. Events are keyed on the station, transactionId and seqNo, and applied once, in seqNo order, whatever the EVSE status. The backend closes a transaction provisionally, at its own last recorded meter value, only when the charger reports it is not ongoing with nothing queued, the event sequence has no gaps, and recorded energy is flat; the invoice is then marked provisional for billing review. Anything else (energy still rising, no ongoing report, a sequence gap, or a newer transaction on the same EVSE) goes to a person. A late Ended after a provisional close replaces the provisional values once and does not create a second charge. Behind a per-station flag on 5 canary sites running FW-B 4.2.x; 6 control sites (4 FW-B, 2 FW-A) stay on the old behaviour, so the control is not perfectly matched. Firmware vendor ticket opened for FW-B behaviour after reconnect; still open.
